correctness.rationale: PASS: Directly recomputed the exact three neighborhood families F_i={x_{i-1},x_{i+1},y_{i-1},y_{i+1}}, T_i={x_{i-1},x_{i+1},z} and Y={all y_j}; K=U union (z*C), with C the original-vertex step-two cycle (odd n gives a single n-cycle) and U intersect (z*C)=C. For n odd >=5, the F_i,Y good simplex cover of U has nerve a cone on the step-two cycle, hence U is contractible. The homotopy pushout of two contractible subcomplexes over C=S^1 is S^2 and the integral Mayer-Vietoris connecting map to H1(C)=Z is an isomorphism. Deleting z leaves U; deleting x_k preserves the F_i,Y nerve and turns C into a path, making both pieces and intersection contractible. Deleting y_k removes exactly the fan triangle (F_{k-1},F_{k+1},Y) but retains its edge via x_k; the punctured fan retracts onto the F_i boundary cycle. Compatible edge covers of C and the F_i subcover give a natural-nerve homotopy equivalence C -> U-y_k, whose cone is contractible. The factorization of any proper induced restriction via a one-vertex deletion then kills its map to ambient integral H2; no assertion about intrinsic homology is necessary. Step-two cycle orientations give rotation +1/reflection -1 on H2 by equivariance. Independent direct mod-two boundary-rank computations checked n=5,7,9 (respectively 92,212,620 nonempty simplices) and all three deletion-orbit representatives: full reduced Betti degree2=1, each deletion acyclic; they do not prove the all-odd integral theorem. Risk: the map of simplex nerves is stated succinctly but compatible contractible simplex intersections make naturality apply in this finite setting; no missed triple intersection was observed in small independent enumerations.

This is not merely the previously known Mycielski suspension or a small finite table; it is a potentially reusable topology-of-induced-restrictions phenomenon.
